---
title: "Scrape: dating services"
engine: knitr
---

The "Comparison of online dating services" table mixes a registered-user count with a reporting year in one free-text cell, and the "Free" and "All features free" columns hold full sentences rather than a plain Yes/No. We save the raw columns as-is here; the parsing happens in [clean_dating.qmd](clean_dating.qmd).

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

In R, `httr2` fetches the page, `rvest::html_table()` parses every table on it, and `Filter()` keeps the one with "Registered users" in its header.

```{r}
#| label: scrape-dating-r
#| eval: false
library(httr2)
library(rvest)
library(readr)

html <- request("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparison_of_online_dating_services") |>
  req_user_agent("wikimill-project/0.1") |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_html()

tables <- html_table(html)
dating <- Filter(\(t) any(grepl("Registered users", names(t))), tables)[[1]]
names(dating) <- c(
  "name", "description", "owner", "registered_users", "free",
  "all_features_free", "hetero", "poly", "free_messaging", "std_notification"
)
write_csv(dating, "data/dating_services.csv")
head(dating)
```

## Python

In Python, `requests` fetches the page, then `pandas.read_html()` finds every table and `match=` picks out the same one.

```{python}
#| label: scrape-dating-py
#| eval: false
import io
import pandas as pd
import requests

dating_html = requests.get(
    "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparison_of_online_dating_services",
    headers={"User-Agent": "wikimill-project/0.1"}
).text
tables = pd.read_html(io.StringIO(dating_html), match="Registered users")
dating = tables[0]
dating.columns = [
    "name", "description", "owner", "registered_users", "free",
    "all_features_free", "hetero", "poly", "free_messaging", "std_notification"
]
dating.to_csv("data/dating_services.csv", index=False)
dating.head()
```

:::

::: {.callout-note}

## Which language should I use?

Both versions take about the same code and keep the same table:

* `rvest::html_table()` returns every table on the page, and `Filter()` keeps the one whose header mentions "Registered users".

* `pandas.read_html()` does the same filtering in one step with `match=`.

The raw text stays as-is in both CSVs, so the cleaning step parses the same strings either way.

:::

These chunks are shown for reference only (`eval: false`), so rendering the site doesn't hit Wikipedia. Run `Rscript src/scrape_dating.R` or `python src/scrape_dating.py` from the project root to refresh `data/dating_services.csv`.
